name: Veneers
tagline: Real timber, thin enough to specify by the sheet
description: Veneer is how a project gets genuine wood without genuine wood budgets or movement. The choice is between natural veneer — unique, variable, needs matching — and reconstituted or engineered veneer, which repeats predictably across a large run. Every sheet here is specified with species, cut, match and finish.

materials.name: Natural veneer
materials.blurb: Sliced from a real log — every leaf unique
materials.description: The genuine article: thin timber sliced from a log and laid on board. Colour and figure vary sheet to sheet, so order the full requirement from one bundle and plan the match on the drawing before cutting.

materials.name: Reconstituted veneer
materials.blurb: Engineered from fast-growing timber for a repeatable grain
materials.description: Fast-grown wood is dyed, laminated and re-sliced to a consistent grain, so sheet 40 matches sheet 1. The pragmatic choice for large runs, hotel rooms and anywhere the client cannot tolerate variation.

materials.name: Engineered veneer
materials.blurb: Designed grain patterns unavailable in nature
materials.description: Same technology as reconstituted veneer, used deliberately for graphic effect — extra-wide straight grain, tight ripple, colour-shifted greys. Gives a contemporary, controlled look no natural log will hold.

materials.name: Pre-finished veneer
materials.blurb: Factory-polished — no site polishing, no smell, no delay
materials.description: Arrives sealed and cured in a factory line, so the carpenter cuts, bands and installs with no polishing trade on site. Removes a week of dust and fumes from a live-in renovation.

materials.name: Teak veneer
materials.blurb: The Indian classic — warm gold-brown, ages beautifully
materials.description: Burma and African teak remain the default premium species in Indian homes, especially for main doors and pooja units. Rich golden brown when new, deepening with age and oil.

materials.name: Oak veneer
materials.blurb: Open-pore, pale and contemporary — the current favourite
materials.description: European and American oak in natural, smoked and white-washed variants. The open pore reads beautifully in matte finishes and suits the pale Scandinavian palettes clients keep asking for.

materials.name: Walnut veneer
materials.blurb: Deep chocolate brown with dramatic figure
materials.description: American walnut brings depth and quiet luxury — the species to specify for a study, a bar or a formal living room. Expensive, and worth planning the layout around so the figure runs continuously.

materials.name: Ash veneer
materials.blurb: Very pale, strong grain — excellent under stain
materials.description: Almost white with a pronounced grain that takes stain evenly, so it can be pushed grey, black or warm without losing figure. A designer's blank canvas.

materials.name: Maple veneer
materials.blurb: Fine, near-uniform grain in a creamy blond
materials.description: Subtle and even — used where the timber should recede and the form should lead. Popular in minimal wardrobes and kids' rooms where a busy grain would be a distraction.

materials.name: Rosewood veneer
materials.blurb: Dark, richly figured Indian classic for statement joinery
materials.description: Sheesham and allied species deliver deep purple-brown tones with strong dark streaks. Traditional in Indian homes for door panels and heirloom furniture; check the source paperwork on protected species.

materials.name: Mahogany veneer
materials.blurb: Warm reddish brown with a fine ribbon figure
materials.description: A traditional joinery timber with a red undertone that warms a room under yellow light. Suits classical detailing, panelled libraries and period-reference work.

materials.name: Ebony veneer
materials.blurb: Near-black timber for the strongest contrast in a scheme
materials.description: Dense, dark and expensive — used in slivers rather than sheets. A single ebony reveal or handle detail does more work than an entire wall of a cheaper species.

materials.name: Smoked veneer
materials.blurb: Fumed timber — colour driven right through the sheet
materials.description: Ammonia fuming darkens the wood chemically rather than with stain, so the tone runs through the leaf and sanding will not expose a pale line. Gives smoked oak its characteristic depth.
